projects.name: Hercules
researchedFrom: Hercules (Apache-2.0) has no release tags. A version is the watermark its source writes: v1.5 (from 2024-09-22), v1.6 (2024-11-03), v1.6.2 (2025-01-27), v2.0.0  [https://github.com/zeusssz/hercules-obfuscator; high: the tool's own source]

Two virtual-machine formats exist. 1.5 and 1.6 use modules/Compiler/c.lua; 1.6.2 and 2.x use VMGenerator.lua with Compiler/Serializer.lua: Lua 5.1 bytecode, ser [https://github.com/zeusssz/hercules-obfuscator (src/modules/VMGenerator.lua, Compiler/Serializer.lua, Compiler/VMStrings.lua); high]

Serializer.lua writes no bytes for a nil constant but the count includes it (`#` stops at a nil), so the interpreter reads the next tag as this one's and the sc [tests/corpus/obfuscated/hercules (s02, s06 virtual_machine); high: reproduced]

versions.note: last commit whose watermark says v1.5 (2024-11-03): first virtual machine (Compiler/c.lua), StringToExpressions, WrapInFunction, compressor
first commit whose watermark says v1.5 (2024-09-22): text modules only, no virtual machine
last commit whose watermark says v1.6 (2025-01-25): anti_tamper added
last commit whose watermark says v1.6.2 (2026-04-30)
last commit whose watermark says v2.0.0 (2026-06-16): manifest.lua, presets, rewritten compiler (Compiler/*.lua)

projects.name: Obscura
researchedFrom: README and git history read as text; the three revisions were then run in tests/corpus/tools/sandbox_run.py (no network, no host files) through gen_obscura.py

Obscura (MIT, Python, vo3pal) is a Luau obfuscator with modes lightweight, rename, native and vm; versions 1.0.0 (pre-hardening), 1.0.1 (2026-04-30, VM hardenin [https://github.com/vo3pal/obscura; high for the history; nothing measured]

versions.note: the state before the VM hardening release (2026-04-29): VM with an encrypted constant pool, --level 1-4, --vm
v1.0.1 (2026-04-30): VM hardening (lazy constants, split keys, integrity checks), --vm-hardening
v1.1.0 (2026-10-08): --mode lightweight/rename/native/vm, rolling bytecode reads by default

improvements.summary: math.floor / math.ceil of an integer literal is the literal (the number layer wraps every number in it), so bit32.bxor(math.floor(a), math.floor(b)) folds and the control-flow flattener's next states become constants
a closure called on the spot that only computes a constant from constants is that constant (the opaque predicates `(function() local n = 22 return n * n < 0 end)()`)
tests: tests/formats-ix.test.mjs: simplify: a closure called on the spot

improvements.summary: a flattened function inside another function's body is unflattened: a leaf that returns or raises the `error("CFF Error: Invalid state")` else no longer counts against the machine, and a loop of two blocks that cannot end on its own is read (closes KNOWN-ISSUES 27 for this shape)
a table of untouched globals read only by constant keys (the table-indirection layer, also `math.pi`) is inlined, whatever its name looks like; a numeric statement nobody keeps (`math.cos(12)`) goes
tests: tests/formats-ix.test.mjs: simplify: a table of builtins

improvements.summary: the run of executor-detection ifs at the top (1.1.0: empty error; 1.0.x: "Security violation" messages, in a do block) is taken off when at least two are present and one probes an executor-only global

lightweight mode decrypts its string table in place (`T[k] = D(T[k], key, i)`): the decoder call is seeded with the stored text, evaluated, and the reads and the copies the obfuscator made (`local a = T[1]`) become the strings
a function that reads or slices a string, mixes it with bxor and builds text with string.char is a decoder from its first call, however it is wrapped (a script with two hidden strings has two calls)
the reference-runtime oracle no longer dies on a recovered file whose report header holds a real Unicode character (it used to take every later request with it)

failurePatterns.summary: the VM builds keep the program as bytecode (encrypted constant pool, rolling reads) for a generated interpreter. Identified from the "Obscura VM" header, reported as not recovered; no lifter was written
failurePatterns.evidence: fidelity 3% before and after on all three revisions; the report header says so

failurePatterns.summary: identifier renaming is not reversible: samples whose original names are descriptive (s02, s03, s06) lose fidelity that no pass can win back; the structure is recovered
failurePatterns.evidence: the remaining differences in s02/s03/s06 are names and inlined named constants

failurePatterns.summary: Obscura 1.0.0 fails with a Lexer error on one sample (s03); recorded as tool-error in its manifest, never counted as a recovery

assumptions: Only the three revisions named were run; earlier history was read, not run
Behaviour is checked on Luau 0.739 (the vendored binary), not in Roblox: `game`, `workspace` and the Roblox API come from the oracle's mock environment

projects.name: RBXLuaObfuscator
researchedFrom: RBXLuaObfuscator (kosuke14, no licence, 2022) does not call loadstring: it ships a Lua lexer, parser and interpreter written in Lua and hands it the program as  [https://github.com/kosuke14/RBXLuaObfuscator; high]

projects.name: XFuscator
researchedFrom: README, Obfuscation Scripts and the library (XFuscator/init.lua) read as text; run through run_isolated.py with drivers/xfuscator.lua, which calls XFuscator.XFuscate with the options the command line would set

improvements.summary: the program kept as an array of scaled character codes (`_(99900)`, scale = a random number drawn at build time) is read by finding the scale that makes every entry divide and the text parse; the wrapper (globals table, tamper check, clock-seeded generator) goes
`string.char(d(n))` where d is a XOR with a key (the encrypt option, through `bit or bit32 or require'bit'`) is evaluated in the sandbox; `table.concat{ ... }` of the results folds to the string

failurePatterns.summary: the precompile step reads Lua 5.1 bytecode through LAT, which reads every integer as a size_t: it only works on 32-bit builds. This host is 64-bit, so no precompiled output was generated and none is claimed
the tool itself fails with those options (Step2.lua:11 concatenates nil, init.lua:110 indexes nil): recorded as tool-error
locals are renamed (s02, s05, s06 lose their descriptive names)

assumptions: Output of XFuscator 2013 'Version 2.0 b1' only; there are 8 commits and the last one was run

projects.name: LuaXen
researchedFrom: README and examples/obfuscator-example.lua read as text; run through run_isolated.py with drivers/luaxen.lua (the call the example makes)

improvements.summary: numbers hidden as `setmetatable({}, {__op = function(_, a) local x, y, z = a[1], a[2], a[3] return x*x - y*y + z end}) <op> {x, y, z}` are evaluated without running anything; the same trick with a loop that builds strings from triples is evaluated in the sandbox when every name in it is declared inside or a standard global
a `while` whose body always leaves it is an `if` (the AST stage writes its conditionals this way)
the state loops of the AST stage (`while 0.69 do if state == ...`, as few as two blocks) are unflattened

failurePatterns.summary: IronBrikked, the VM stage (LZW-compressed encoded prototype and an interpreter), is identified and reported as not recovered; with `both` the AST layer over it is peeled and the VM remains
the tool raised `No loop to break` on s04 in both configurations; recorded as tool-error

assumptions: Only the single commit of the repository was run; `legacy/` was not touched

projects.name: Zartha
researchedFrom: README, Main.lua, Pipeline.lua and the Vm tree read as text; run through run_isolated.py with drivers/zartha.lua, which does in memory what Pipeline.lua does (luac replaced by string.dump)

failurePatterns.summary: a per-build Lua 5.1 bytecode VM with generated opcodes: identified (watermark and the `Env["string"]["char"]` prelude) and flagged as not recovered; no lifter was written
luasrcdiet inside the tool fails on s06 in both configurations that minify (an unexpected backslash); recorded as tool-error

assumptions: The watermark text is a setting (`File generated using [Zartha]` is the default), so it is evidence and not proof; the prelude rule is the structural one

projects.name: FusGato v1
researchedFrom: README and the source read as text; the Luvit program was run through run_isolated.py with drivers/fusgato.lua (stand-ins for Luvit's fs, json and relative require; the compile is string.dump)

improvements.summary: the IronBrew watermark FusGato copies does not make it IronBrew 2: the credit line decides, and the VM is flagged as not rebuilt (before this it was reported as recovered with confidence high)
tests: tests/formats-ix.test.mjs: luaxen IronBrikked, zartha and fusgato

failurePatterns.summary: the author calls it half-working: vm/opcodes/24.lua has no `return`, so 12 of 16 builds fail with `attempt to index local 'opcode'`; the 4 outputs that were written run but do not reproduce the original's output (diverged)
the outputs are IronBrew-style VMs; identified, not recovered

assumptions: The relative-require resolution of the driver (every module directory tried when a tail call hides the caller) is ours; it was checked on the one build that completes

projects.name: RealObfuscator
researchedFrom: README, Cargo.toml and docs read as text; the 166 crates were downloaded with `cargo vendor` (no build script of theirs ran on the host), the tool was built offline in the sandbox and run only there (gen_realobf.py)

improvements.summary: the sandbox walks `for k, v in t do` over a table without __iter (Luau); the lightweight mode's eager-decoding loop made the whole evaluation fail before
a number held by a randomly named local is an obfuscator's key and goes where it is used; `(bit32.op(...) + k) - k` is the bit32 result
a VM build is recognised by its pool of dozens of encoded records and flagged as not rebuilt

failurePatterns.summary: register bytecode with shuffled records, opcode aliases and lazy constants: identified, not recovered
the VM rule counts records (40 or more in a build over 20 kB); a lightweight build of a program with that many strings would be flagged as a VM although it is recovered

assumptions: Version 2.2.1 (revision 9ec569f) only; the repository's earlier Python versions were not run
Behaviour checked on Luau; fixtures are not committed (GPL), so the measurements reproduce only with the same build

projects.name: zynaa/LuaObfuscator
researchedFrom: README and the Python source read as text; both commits run through gen_zynaa.py in sandbox_run.py with the random generator seeded and the clipboard switched off

improvements.summary: a decoder written for LuaJIT / Garry's Mod (`bit.bxor`) is evaluated: when the Luau sandbox lacks `bit` the run is repeated as LuaJIT
`local G = _G` read only as `G.name` / `G["name"]` is the global itself (the tool routes every global through such an alias and spells the names with its decoder)
tests: data/research/format-notes.json (covered by the zynaa fixtures when present)

failurePatterns.summary: on LuaJIT s03 is rejected as invalid syntax ("')' expected") and s05 stops with a runtime error ("arithmetic on a nil value") after printing part of its output, at every level, in both commits; the fixtures are recorded as errored in their manifests and are not counted as recovery failures
s06: the tool's string stripper aborts ("Failed to correctly strip strings"); no output was written
s07 (Roblox-style): the sandbox evaluation fails because `game` is not defined in it, so the decoded strings of that sample are not read

assumptions: The tool was written for Garry's Mod; Roblox-style samples are outside what it was made for

projects.name: Luarmor loader
researchedFrom: seven files of the public collection's Unknown folder read as text; nothing fetched

improvements.summary: scripts that only download and run code are classified as remote loaders and the report says the program is not in the file and is not fetched; Luarmor's bootstrap is identified from its header comment and its cdn host

failurePatterns.summary: the protected program is downloaded from the service when the script runs; it is not in the file, and getting it past the service's access control is not something this tool does

assumptions: The bootstrap shape was read on seven files; other Luarmor builds may differ

backlog.item: Unknown / VM Compressed / MinifiedLua folders of the public collection
backlog.detail: every file now has a class (remote loader, remote-library script, plain or minified script, numeric-array loader, Luarmor bootstrap, credit entry ...) instead of 'unidentified'; see data/research/corpus-eval.json classOfUnidentified

backlog.item: A program stored as an array of numbers and run through a local alias of loadstring
backlog.detail: layers.js accepts an alias of loadstring and an indirect final call (`if type(f) == 'function' then ... P() end`); the payload of the sampled file is itself a remote loader

backlog.item: Flattened functions inside other function bodies (KNOWN-ISSUES 27)
backlog.detail: Obscura level-2/3 and LuaXen AST stage; MoonVeil's nested case is unchanged

backlog.item: Luraph files without a version banner (15 of 218)
backlog.detail: 12 of the 15 are classified as minified scripts and 2 as plain scripts, which supports the earlier finding that some files filed under Luraph are other scripts; no new Luraph signature was added

backlog.item: Per-build bytecode VMs (Obscura VM, Zartha, FusGato, IronBrikked, RealObfuscator vm)
backlog.detail: each is flagged unrecoverable so that the report cannot say 'recovered'; none has a lifter
